reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses TiC-reinforced tungsten, not W–Cu composites or copper network formation. It provides no support for any of the key premises about directional solidification, copper connectivity, or thermal conductivity enhancement in W–Cu systems.
premises: Directional solidification can create a continuous, aligned copper network in W–Cu composites.
A continuous copper network reduces interfacial thermal resistance and boosts thermal conductivity.
The tungsten matrix retains mechanical durability and irradiation resistance despite the intervention.
The composite will outperform a standard W–Cu composite in thermal conductivity without degrading other properties.
